items.say: Think about the last time someone said your name kindly. Not shouted across a room, or read off a list, but spoken by someone who was glad you were there.
There's a passage in Isaiah where God does exactly that. He speaks to His people by name, and the first thing He says is, "Fear not."

This is a scripture meditation on Isaiah chapter 43. We'll read a few lines at a time, slowly, with room to breathe in between. When the words end, soft music will stay with you for as long as you'd like to rest, pray, or simply sit quietly.
Wherever you are, in the car before work, at the kitchen table, or curled up at the end of the day, let yourself arrive.
Rest your feet flat if you can. Let your hands lie still.
Breathe in slowly.
And breathe out, a little longer than you breathed in.
Isaiah was speaking to people who had every reason to feel forgotten. They had made mistakes, and hard times had followed. And into that moment, God said this:
"But now thus saith the LORD that created thee, O Jacob, and he that formed thee, O Israel, Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine."
Notice how it begins. "But now." Whatever came before, there is a now, and God speaks into it.
He calls Himself the one who created you and formed you. Formed is a potter's word, the way hands shape clay with care and patience. You weren't made in a hurry.
And then three short phrases. Let's hear them one at a time.
I have redeemed thee.
I have called thee by thy name.
Thou art mine.
If you'd like, say your own name quietly now, and hear it the way God says it. Not as a reminder of everything you have to do, but as someone who belongs to Him.
The next verse is one people hold onto in hard seasons.

"When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee: when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee."
Read it carefully, because it's honest. It doesn't say "if" you pass through the waters. It says "when." Deep water and hard places are part of most lives.
What God offers here isn't a life without rivers. It's His company in the middle of them. "I will be with thee."
Maybe you're in deep water right now. A diagnosis in the family. A marriage under strain. A job that ended. A loneliness that won't lift.
Picture yourself standing in a wide river. The water is moving, and it's cold. But there's someone beside you, holding your arm, steady on His feet. The water rises, but it does not carry you away.
Stay in that picture for a moment. You're not crossing alone.
A little further on, verse 4 begins with words that many people find hard to believe about themselves.
"Since thou wast precious in my sight, thou hast been honourable, and I have loved thee:"
Precious. Honourable. Loved.
Some of us can say those words easily about our children, or our friends, but not about ourselves. We know our own failures too well.

But God isn't describing what you've achieved. He's telling you how He sees you. You are precious in His sight. That isn't something you earn this week, and it isn't something you can lose by having a bad day.
Let's sit with one word. Precious.
Let it land somewhere quiet inside you.

chapters.title: Fear not, for I am with thee

items.say: Verse 5 begins by repeating the first promise, almost like a parent saying it twice, so a frightened child really hears it.
"Fear not: for I am with thee:"
Notice the reason given for not being afraid. It isn't that every problem is solved. It isn't that you are strong enough. The reason is simply, "I am with thee."
So let's breathe with these words.
Breathing in: Fear not.
Breathing out: You are with me.
Breathing in: Fear not.
Breathing out: You are with me.
Keep that rhythm on your own for a few breaths, if it helps.
Later in the chapter, God speaks to people who were stuck looking backwards.

"Remember ye not the former things, neither consider the things of old. Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert."
This doesn't ask us to forget the past or pretend it didn't hurt. It asks us not to live there. Not to let what went wrong before decide what God can do next.
Notice the picture. A way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert. Not the end of the wilderness, but a path through it. Not rain everywhere at once, but water where there wasn't any.
New things often start small. A first green shoot is easy to miss. That is why God asks, "shall ye not know it?" So let's ask for eyes to notice.
Is there one small sign of life, of kindness, or of hope in your week that you almost walked past? Think of it now.
Let's pray.

Lord, You formed me, and You call me by my name. Thank You that I am Yours. When I pass through deep waters this week, be with me, and don't let them carry me away. Help me believe that I am precious in Your sight, even on the days I don't feel it. Quiet my fears with Your nearness. And open my eyes to the new things You are growing, even in the dry places. In Jesus' name, Amen.

Thank you for spending this time with us. If you'd like us to pray for you, you're welcome to leave your first name and a short prayer request in the comments. Now just rest. The music will stay with you. God bless you.
